html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. SOP: standard operating procedure; KPI: key performance indicator

  • What efficiency and effectiveness mean for a Claude workflow
  • How to save time and usage with prompts, Projects, models and settings
  • How to standardize and share what works
  • How to measure and improve over time

2Efficiency and Effectiveness

Running case

Cedarbrook's Monthly Report

  • Finance spends two days a month building the sales report: pulling numbers, writing commentary, formatting slides
  • After optimization the team uses one Project, a saved method for the report format, a lighter model for the commentary draft and one review pass; the work takes half a day, and the number of corrections falls
  • Efficiency = the same result with less time, effort and usage.
  • Effectiveness = a better result: accurate, useful, on-brand, accepted by the reader.
  • Optimize both. A fast but wrong report is not an improvement, and a perfect report that takes five days is not either.
  • Optimize where it matters: frequent tasks, slow tasks, error-prone tasks.

3The Main Levers

Lever What to do Why it helps
Better prompts Specific goal, audience, format; examples; batch related requests into one message Fewer rounds; less usage
Reuse Save good prompts in a prompt library; use Projects and Skills for recurring work Consistency; no re-typing; shared knowledge
Project knowledge Upload reference documents once; project content is cached and counts less when reused Fewer tokens per question
Right model Lighter model for routine and high-volume tasks; stronger for hard work (Module 7) Speed and usage savings
Right effort Lower effort for routine tasks; higher only for complex ones Faster; stretches usage limits
Right feature Chat for light tasks; web search for facts; Research only for deep work Avoids expensive over-tooling
Fewer tools on Turn off connectors and web search you do not need ("tools and connectors are token-intensive") More room in the context; less usage
Short chats Start fresh for new topics; summarize long threads (Module 8) Shorter context, lower usage, better focus
Lean instructions Keep Project instructions short; put task-specific details in the chat Less context overhead
Targeted edits Edit one section instead of regenerating everything Saves time and usage
Process design Remove unnecessary hand-offs; add review where errors matter; draft-and-review patterns (Module 10) Faster and safer

Usage factors: message length, attachment size, conversation length, tools (Research, web search), model choice, effort level, artifact creation and multi-step tasks such as file creation. Caches expire after inactivity, so the first message after a long break costs more.

Exam tip

Efficiency answers pick the lighter, reusable, batched option (a Project, a lighter model for routine work, fewer tools, a new short chat), and keep quality checks in place.

4Standardize and Share What Works

  • Turn successful prompts into templates with blanks (audience, topic, key facts).
  • Put the team's voice, rules and reference documents in a shared Project (Team and Enterprise allow sharing with view or edit rights).
  • Package a repeatable method as a Skill.
  • Write a short SOP: when to use Claude for this task, the steps, who reviews, what to check.
  • Keep an owner and a version; review monthly.
  • Train colleagues with real examples of good and bad outputs.
Without standardization With standardization
Every person writes their own prompt Shared template and Project
Quality depends on the person Consistent baseline
Fixes stay in one head Lessons shared and recorded

5Measure and Improve

KPI How to measure Target example
Time per task Stopwatch or ticket timestamps Report in 4 hours, not 16
Error rate Share of outputs needing factual corrections Under 5%
Rework rounds Average number of revisions 1 or 2
Usage Share of the session or weekly limit used Under planned budget
Satisfaction Reader or colleague rating At least 4 of 5
  1. Baseline: measure the current way.
  2. Change one thing.
  3. Pilot with a few users.
  4. Compare against the baseline.
  5. Keep or revert; roll out if it works.
  6. Repeat, because tools, policies and needs change.
  • Watch quality as well as speed: a quicker draft with more factual errors is not an improvement.
  • Check in regularly on settings and knowledge so the gains do not decay (Module 12).
Exam tip

Efficiency without quality checks is not optimization: measure speed and error rate.

Exam tip

Reuse beats re-typing: Projects, Skills and templates save time and usage and keep results consistent.

6Exam Q&A

S1A team sends dozens of short, similar customer replies every day and keeps hitting its usage limit. Which change helps most?

  • AMake every chat as long as possible
  • BUse the most capable model at the highest effort, since quality should never be traded for usage
  • CAdd every connector
  • DUse a lighter model with lower effort, with a Project that holds the reply rules
Show the answer

Answer: D. Routine, high-volume work suits a lighter setup and shared context.

S2A manager wants quicker monthly reporting. What should come first?

  • ARemove review steps
  • BSwitch tools randomly
  • CAsk Claude to promise faster results
  • DMeasure the current time and error rate, then change one element and compare
Show the answer

Answer: D. Measuring the current time and error rate first gives a baseline, so one change at a time can be compared fairly against it.

S3Which action reduces unnecessary usage?

  • AStarting very long chats for everything so that no context is ever lost
  • BKeeping many connectors on in every chat so Claude always has everything within reach
  • CAlways selecting maximum effort
  • DTurning off connectors and web search that the task does not need
Show the answer

Answer: D. Tools and connectors consume context and usage, so turning off the ones a task does not need reduces unnecessary consumption.

S4A user returns to a Project after a long break, and the first message seems to use more of the limit. Why?

  • AProjects are broken after a long break and have to be recreated before the usage meter behaves normally
  • BThe model changed
  • CProject content is cached, and the cache expires after inactivity, so the content counts in full again
  • DMemory is full
Show the answer

Answer: C. Caching saves usage while active; it lapses after inactivity.

S5Which TWO help standardize good results across a team? Select TWO.

  • ALetting each person improvise
  • BAvoiding documentation
  • CHiding the best prompts
  • DA shared Project with instructions and approved knowledge
  • EA shared template in a prompt library
Show the answer

Answer: D, E. Shared templates and a shared Project with approved knowledge spread what works, so quality does not depend on one person.

S6Draft time fell by half, but factual corrections doubled. What does this show?

  • AA measurement error that can be ignored, because the figures will even out again next month
  • BA clear success
  • CThe model is too small, so the team should switch to the largest model and stop reviewing drafts
  • DEfficiency improved while accuracy got worse, so the process needs a better check or prompt
Show the answer

Answer: D. Speed improved but accuracy got worse, so effectiveness fell; the process needs a better check or a clearer prompt.

S7Which is the most efficient way to change one paragraph in a long document artifact?

  • AHighlight the paragraph and ask Claude to edit just that part
  • BStart a new chat and re-upload all of the source material from scratch
  • CDelete the artifact
  • DRegenerate the entire document from the start and compare it with the old version
Show the answer

Answer: A. Highlighting the paragraph and asking for an edit of just that part saves time and usage and leaves the rest untouched.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Goal Efficiency (less time and usage) and effectiveness (better results)
Prompts Specific, reused, batched
Reuse Prompt library · Projects · Skills
Model and effort Lighter and lower for routine; stronger and higher for hard
Tools Turn off connectors and search you do not need
Chats Short and focused; restart with a summary
Cache Saves usage while active; expires after inactivity
Standardize Templates · shared Project · SOP · owner · training
Measure Baseline · change one thing · pilot · compare · keep or revert
KPIs Time · error rate · rework rounds · usage · satisfaction
